## Features

- **Starter keypad pages.** tmux-legion now carries a set of keypad pages inside the binary: Escape, mute, backspace, Danish letters, and shift on the first page, `/quit` and Enter on the second. When the sidebar opens with the keypad backend on and `~/.config/tmux-legion/keypad.json` doesn't exist yet, tmux-legion writes them there for you to edit, so a fresh install on another Mac has pages right away. It never overwrites an existing file. Use `{ "pages": [] }` to keep just the agents page. The pages are also in the repo as [keypad/keypad.json](https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion/blob/v0.9.0/keypad/keypad.json).

## Maintenance

- Builds against [mx-keypad v0.8.0](https://github.com/hawkish/mx-keypad/releases/tag/v0.8.0). That release writes its own starter config to `~/.config/mx-keypad/config.json` the first time `mx-keypad run` or `install` finds none there.

## Install

### Nix flake

```nix
# Pin to a release tag (recommended); drop the ref to track the default branch.
inputs.tmux-legion.url = "github:hawkish/tmux-legion/v0.9.0";
```

### Manual and TPM-style

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion
cd ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion && cargo build --release
echo 'run-shell ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion/tmux-legion.tmux' >> ~/.tmux.conf
```

Upgrading needs a tmux config reload, not just a rebuild — see [After upgrading](https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion#after-upgrading). The [README](https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion#install) covers Claude Code hooks, the agent skill, and the pi extension.
